What is an eSIM?

An eSIM is a digital SIM that's already built into most modern smartphones. It works like a physical SIM card, but you don't need to insert anything into your device. eSIMs come with many perks, such as helping you avoid roaming fees and making it simple to switch between providers.

Frequently asked questions about eSIMs for the UK

Yes! You can get an eSIM for the UK, but make sure your device is eSIM-compatible before purchasing. Besides, you don’t have to be in the UK to buy one. With Saily, you can purchase your UK eSIM from anywhere in the world, and it will automatically activate when you arrive. Unlike traditional SIM cards, there’s no need to visit a store, wait for delivery, or pick it up at a physical location — you’re connected the moment you land.

One key drawback is that not all devices are eSIM-compatible, so you’ll need to check if your phone supports it before buying an eSIM data plan. Troubleshooting can also be trickier since you can’t simply remove and reinsert a SIM card to reset your connection. Additionally, eSIM functionality depends on your device’s operating system, and compatibility can vary between manufacturers and carriers. However, the convenience, security, and flexibility of eSIMs make them a game-changer for most travelers and digital nomads.

Switching from a physical SIM to an eSIM is simple, but the process depends on your carrier. Most major UK networks allow you to request an eSIM through their app or customer support. Typically, you'll receive a QR code that you can scan to activate your new eSIM profile. Once set up, your old SIM will be deactivated, and you’ll be able to enjoy the benefits of having an eSIM. For a step-by-step guide, check out our article on how to convert a physical SIM to an eSIM.

Setting up an eSIM in the UK is quick and easy. Here’s how you can do it:

  • Make sure your phone is eSIM-compatible.

  • Purchase an eSIM plan from Saily.

  • Check your email for a QR code or activation details.

  • Open your phone’s settings and navigate to the eSIM or mobile data section.

  • Scan the QR code or enter the activation details manually.

  • Follow the on-screen instructions to complete the setup.

Once activated, your eSIM will connect to the network, and you’re good to go! For a more detailed guide, check out how to install eSIM on Android or iPhone.

It all depends on your needs — factors like price, duration, data allowance, and network coverage all play a role in finding the right fit. However, Saily stands out by offering some of the most competitive pricing while maintaining top-tier eSIM quality. Whether you're looking for a short-term plan for a quick trip or a larger data package for extended stays, Saily ensures reliable connectivity at great value.

While getting a local eSIM in the UK might seem like the most straightforward option, there are a few drawbacks to consider. Most eSIM providers for the UK primarily offer monthly paid plans, making it difficult for short-term travelers to find a flexible, prepaid option. Some networks do provide pay-as-you-go eSIMs, but choices are limited. That’s why Saily is a great alternative for travelers heading to the UK. With prepaid plans that you can easily top up, you get the flexibility to choose the data package that fits your travel needs.

Yes, 5G is available on eSIMs in the UK, but it depends on the provider and network coverage. Some local carriers offer 5G, while others may limit speeds to 4G/LTE. With the Saily eSIM app, you can enjoy fast and reliable 5G connectivity in the UK, ensuring smoother browsing, streaming, and video calls wherever 5G is available.

There are several reasons why your eSIM for the UK might be running slower than expected. Network congestion, signal interference, or technical issues with your device or the carrier can all play a role. If your eSIM supports multiple networks, switching to a different one may improve your connection. Also, make sure you're in an area with strong coverage and that your device settings allow for the fastest available speeds.

No. An eSIM itself doesn’t use more battery than a physical SIM. However, if you’re running two lines at once — an eSIM and a physical SIM — your phone has to maintain a connection to two networks. That can lead to slightly higher battery usage, but for most users, the difference is barely noticeable.

eSIM technology is still relatively new, and like any emerging tech, it takes time for widespread adoption. While more and more devices now support eSIMs, many people are still used to traditional physical SIM cards and may not be aware of the benefits eSIMs offer. As the technology continues to grow, more carriers and users are expected to make the switch, making eSIMs a standard option in the near future.

Yes, eSIMs are more difficult to hack than traditional physical SIM cards. This is due to the advanced encryption and security protocols integrated into eSIM technology. While some vulnerabilities, such as software-based attacks and phishing, exist, unlike physical SIM cards, eSIMs eliminate the risks associated with SIM swapping or theft. For an even safer browsing experience, Saily offers additional eSIM security features, such as web protection, an ad blocker, and virtual locations.

Not necessarily, but it depends on your needs. While VPNs provide encryption and additional privacy features that enhance your digital security, the Saily eSIM app offers its own set of security features, such as a virtual location, which can further boost your privacy. This makes Saily a strong option for those seeking added privacy. However, if you require the full range of encryption and other advanced privacy protections, using a VPN alongside an eSIM might still be a good choice.

While there is no such thing as a completely free eSIM, you can earn free Saily credits through our Saily referral program. After a few successful referrals, you can get a Saily eSIM data plan completely free of charge.

What is an eSIM?
An
eSIM
is a digital SIM that's already built into most modern smartphones. It works like a physical SIM card, but you don't need to insert anything into your device. eSIMs come with many perks, such as helping you avoid roaming fees and making it simple to switch between providers.

Frequently asked questions about eSIMs for the UK
Can I get an eSIM in the UK?
Yes! You can get an eSIM for the UK, but make sure your device is eSIM-compatible before purchasing. Besides, you don’t have to be in the UK to buy one. With Saily, you can purchase your UK eSIM from anywhere in the world, and it will automatically activate when you arrive. Unlike traditional SIM cards, there’s no need to visit a store, wait for delivery, or pick it up at a physical location — you’re connected the moment you land.
What are the disadvantages of an eSIM?
One key drawback is that not all devices are eSIM-compatible, so you’ll need to check if your phone supports it before buying an eSIM data plan. Troubleshooting can also be trickier since you can’t simply remove and reinsert a SIM card to reset your connection. Additionally, eSIM functionality depends on your device’s operating system, and compatibility can vary between manufacturers and carriers. However, the convenience, security, and flexibility of eSIMs make them a game-changer for most travelers and digital nomads.
How can you convert a SIM to an eSIM?
Switching from a physical SIM to an eSIM is simple, but the process depends on your carrier. Most major UK networks allow you to request an eSIM through their app or customer support. Typically, you'll receive a QR code that you can scan to activate your new eSIM profile. Once set up, your old SIM will be deactivated, and you’ll be able to enjoy the benefits of having an eSIM. For a step-by-step guide, check out our article on how to
convert a physical SIM to an eSIM
.

Check your email for a QR code or activation details.
Open your phone’s settings and navigate to the eSIM or mobile data section.
Scan the QR code or enter the activation details manually.
Follow the on-screen instructions to complete the setup.

Should I get a local eSIM provider in the UK?
While getting a local eSIM in the UK might seem like the most straightforward option, there are a few drawbacks to consider. Most eSIM providers for the UK primarily offer monthly paid plans, making it difficult for short-term travelers to find a flexible, prepaid option. Some networks do provide pay-as-you-go eSIMs, but choices are limited. That’s why Saily is a great alternative for travelers heading to the UK. With prepaid plans that you can easily top up, you get the flexibility to choose the data package that fits your travel needs.
Does an eSIM in the UK have 5G?
Yes, 5G is available on eSIMs in the UK, but it depends on the provider and network coverage. Some local carriers offer 5G, while others may limit speeds to 4G/LTE. With the Saily eSIM app, you can enjoy fast and reliable 5G connectivity in the UK, ensuring smoother browsing, streaming, and video calls wherever 5G is available.
Why is my eSIM in the UK so slow?
There are several reasons why your eSIM for the UK might be running slower than expected. Network congestion, signal interference, or technical issues with your device or the carrier can all play a role. If your eSIM supports multiple networks, switching to a different one may improve your connection. Also, make sure you're in an area with strong coverage and that your device settings allow for the fastest available speeds.
Does an eSIM drain the battery?
No. An eSIM itself doesn’t use more battery than a physical SIM. However, if you’re running two lines at once — an eSIM and a physical SIM — your phone has to maintain a connection to two networks. That can lead to slightly higher battery usage, but for most users, the difference is barely noticeable.
Why are eSIMs not popular?
eSIM technology is still relatively new, and like any emerging tech, it takes time for widespread adoption. While more and more devices now support eSIMs, many people are still used to traditional physical SIM cards and may not be aware of the benefits eSIMs offer. As the technology continues to grow, more carriers and users are expected to make the switch, making eSIMs a standard option in the near future.
Is an eSIM harder to hack?
Yes, eSIMs are more difficult to hack than traditional physical SIM cards. This is due to the advanced encryption and security protocols integrated into eSIM technology. While some vulnerabilities, such as software-based attacks and phishing, exist, unlike physical SIM cards, eSIMs eliminate the risks associated with SIM swapping or theft. Do you need a VPN with an eSIM?
Not necessarily, but it depends on your needs. While VPNs provide encryption and additional privacy features that enhance your digital security, the Saily eSIM app offers its own set of security features, such as a virtual location, which can further boost your privacy. This makes Saily a strong option for those seeking added privacy. However, if you require the full range of encryption and other advanced privacy protections, using a VPN alongside an eSIM might still be a good choice.
